title: Dangerous JavaScript and TypeScript security sinks
attackSurface: JavaScript and TypeScript source files scanned for injection-prone security sinks

hostile.title: Direct eval sink
hostile.why: Dynamic code execution of attacker-controlled text

hostile.title: new Function sink
hostile.why: The Function constructor is another dynamic JavaScript evaluation sink

hostile.title: innerHTML injection sink
hostile.why: Unsanitized HTML assignment creates DOM cross-site scripting risk

hostile.title: document.write injection sink
hostile.why: document.write inserts attacker-controlled markup into the document

hostile.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink
hostile.why: React's raw HTML escape hatch is dangerous with user-controlled markup

hostile.title: Template interpolation shell injection
hostile.why: Interpolated shell commands enable command injection

hostile.title: Concatenated shell injection
hostile.why: String-concatenated command arguments enable shell metacharacter injection

hostile.title: TypeScript eval sink
hostile.why: TypeScript source has the same dynamic code execution risk

benign.title: Constant shell command
benign.why: A constant command string has no attacker-controlled interpolation

benign.title: execFile argument array
benign.why: execFile with an argument array avoids shell interpretation

benign.title: JSON parsing
benign.why: JSON parsing is not dynamic JavaScript execution

benign.title: Comment mentioning eval

input.content:
// eval(input) was removed for security reasons.
export const safe = true;

benign.why: Comments are documentation, not executable sinks

benign.title: String mentioning innerHTML

input.content: export const guidance = 'Prefer textContent over innerHTML assignments.';

benign.why: A string mentioning an API is not itself a sink

benign.title: Static template rendering
benign.why: Escaped text interpolation does not use a raw HTML sink

benign.title: TypeScript pure function
benign.why: A pure TypeScript function has no scanned dangerous sink
